items.context: Round 1 settled on adding a progress summary. The segmented bar currently shows colored segments but no text. Other dashboards use either a fraction ('3 of 7') or percentage ('43%') or both. Placement can be above the bar (as a heading supplement) or below (as a caption).

options.label: Fraction below bar: '3 of 7 completed'
options.rationale: Clean, reads naturally, placed as a caption below the progress bar. Matches the mental model of counting items. Recommended because it's the most scannable format for small counts (<50 items).

options.label: Percentage + fraction: '43% (3/7)'
options.rationale: More data-dense. Good for large counts where percentage is more meaningful. But for initiative sizes (typically 3-15 items), the fraction alone is clearer.

options.label: Inline with section header: 'Progress (3/7)'
options.rationale: Compact — puts the count in the header itself. Saves vertical space but makes the header inconsistent with other section headers that are text-only.

items.topic: Specific Lucide icons for section headers
items.context: Round 1 settled on adding icons to Progress and Items headers. Need to lock in exact icon choices. Files already uses FolderOpen. Other detail pages use domain-specific icons (Settings2, Terminal, Clock, etc.). For Progress and Items, several candidates exist in the Lucide library.

options.label: Progress: BarChart3, Items: Layers
options.rationale: BarChart3 visually suggests metrics/progress. Layers suggests stacked items. Both are distinct from FolderOpen and commonly used in dashboard UIs. Recommended for clarity and visual balance.

options.label: Progress: TrendingUp, Items: List
options.rationale: TrendingUp suggests forward motion. List is more literal. But TrendingUp implies growth rather than completion progress, which could be misleading.

options.label: Progress: PieChart, Items: LayoutGrid
options.rationale: PieChart maps to the segmented bar concept. LayoutGrid suggests a structured collection. But PieChart is visually dense at small sizes.

items.topic: Item chip truncation threshold and behavior
items.context: The plan proposes truncating item chips at 12+ items with a '+N more' chip. Need to confirm the threshold and how the overflow chip behaves. Most initiatives have 3-10 items, but some could grow larger.

options.label: Show first 12, then '+N more' as non-interactive muted chip
options.rationale: 12 is enough to see a good cross-section. The '+N more' chip is informational only — users scroll or use the backlog view for the full list. Simple implementation.

options.label: Show first 8, then '+N more' that expands to show all
options.rationale: Lower threshold keeps the card compact. Click-to-expand provides access without navigation. But adds state management and makes the card height unpredictable.

options.label: Show all items, no truncation
options.rationale: Simplest implementation. For the current range of initiative sizes (3-15 items), truncation may never trigger. But future-proofing is lost.

items.context: The current test file (244 lines) uses React Testing Library with assertions on text content, button clicks, and query states. Layout changes (grid, spacing, icons) are harder to test with RTL. Options range from purely structural tests to snapshot-based approaches.

options.label: Behavioral tests only — test presence and interaction, not layout
options.rationale: Test that empty states render when data is empty, kind icons are present via aria-label or test-id, progress summary text appears. Don't test CSS classes or grid structure. Recommended because layout is best verified visually and behavioral tests are more maintainable.

options.label: Behavioral tests + snapshot test for the full page
options.rationale: Snapshot catches unintended layout regressions. But snapshots are brittle — any markup change breaks them, creating maintenance burden.

items.text: The current codebase already imports Lucide icons (Wrench, Play, Lightbulb, CheckSquare, BarChart3, Layers, FolderOpen, Inbox, FileX) in other swarm-manager UI files — no new icon dependencies needed. The BACKLOG_STATUS_CHIP_COLORS mapping and kind-to-icon mapping can be co-located near each other for maintainability.
